description.value: A remote mountain campground on the gravel Whiteswan Forest Service Road within a park anchored by two alpine lakes and Lussier Hot Springs; active mine ore and logging trucks share the narrow canyon section of the access road, making the approach demanding for loaded tourers.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website fetched is BC Parks' overview page for Whiteswan Lake Park, which hosts Inlet Creek Campground as one of five campgrounds but does not name or detail it specifically. OSM tags provide the most granular campground-level data (capacity 16, no power, no internet, no dump station). The 'Book camping' link and reservation policy reference on the BC Parks page support reservations being accepted; power_supply=no and internet_access=no in OSM support denying charging amenities.
concerns: OSM operator is 'EK Parks Ltd.' with email info@ekparks.com, but the linked website is the provincial BC Parks page — the operator relationship and contact details are unclear.
The BC Parks page covers all of Whiteswan Lake Park and does not specifically name or describe Inlet Creek Campground, so campground-level amenities cannot be verified from the website.
Access road is gravel (Whiteswan Forest Service Road) with explicit warnings about mine ore trucks and oversized logging trucks — significant hazard for cyclists.
No cell phone service in the park per website.
Phone number in OSM (+1-250-422-3003) is attributed to EK Parks Ltd. and is not corroborated by the BC Parks website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The campground is legitimate and bookable via BC Parks, but access requires ~25km of rough gravel forest service road shared with heavy industrial trucks, which presents meaningful safety and suitability concerns for touring cyclists. A reviewer should confirm whether cyclists regularly use this route.
enrichment_extras.notes: Canal Flats (nearest community, ~22km away via gravel road) is the closest point for resupply. Lussier Hot Springs within the park may be a notable draw for touring cyclists willing to tackle the access road.

wow_evidence: park anchored by two alpine lakes and Lussier Hot Springs; active mine ore and logging trucks share the narrow canyon section
